model_family: Three precommitted Gaussian factor-copula scenarios with normal log10-leptin and arithmetic-moment-parameterized lognormal positive endpoints

evidence_use.operator: arithmetic means and sample SDs on complete endpoint pairs
evidence_use.population: 44 completers aged 7-14 with simple obesity; before/after 3-month home diet/exercise program with professional follow-up; no randomized parallel arm; 43 glucose and triglyceride pairs.
evidence_use.measurement: units specified per endpoint; pediatric leptin already log10(pg/mL)
evidence_use.reason: Use rounded target-derived arithmetic means and sample SDs as same-population A0 plug-in population moments. They constrain eight univariate marginal distributions, not paired covariance, change SD or cross-endpoint dependence. Finite sample moments fluctuate. Marginal diagnostic agreement is reconstruction compatibility, not independent validation. Leptin is already log10 and is not transformed again.

evidence_use.population: 44 completers aged 7-14 with simple obesity; before/after 3-month home diet/exercise program with professional follow-up; no randomized parallel arm; 43 glucose and triglyceride pairs.
evidence_use.reason: Generate one paired record per independent synthetic completer without a parallel arm. At n=44 retain 44 leptin/body-mass and 43 glucose/triglyceride complete pairs. Round each supplied endpoint count times n/44 for other n. Both-null trailing pairs and shared last-row gaps implement the schema, not a native missingness mechanism. New scenario-specific keys prevent identity confusion.

components.name: source_marginals
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Source means and SDs are treated as fixed population plug-ins, ignoring their sampling and rounding uncertainty. Normal log10-leptin; lognormal mass, glucose and triglycerides with log variance log(1+(sd/mean)^2) and log mean log(mean)-log variance/2. No exact finite-sample moment matching.

components.name: joint_scenario_factors
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Four mutually independent standard Gaussian factor types: shared stable participant, endpoint-specific stable participant, shared participant-visit, and endpoint-visit residual. Squared loadings sum to one in every scenario. Endpoint signs on the visit factor can differ. Positive-semidefinite covariance follows from the factor construction. All shares and signs are explicit assumptions and cannot be estimated from the source marginals.
unresolved_dependencies: Cross-endpoint covariance at and across visits
Six endpoint-change correlations and nonlinear dependence
Whether shared visit variation exists and its endpoint loading signs

components.name: availability_and_identity
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Independent exchangeable synthetic people with new IDs. Fixed trailing complete-pair gaps generalize by scaling counts and do not imply common native missingness. Age, sex, adherence, differential selection and causal effects are not modeled because no supporting summaries are supplied.

scenarios.assumption: Strong stable individual ranking with independent endpoint-visit residual variation and no common visit factor.

next_information_request: Request a privacy-preserving pre/post 8-variable covariance matrix with measurement scales and pairwise sample sizes, or at minimum all four pre/post covariances plus the six covariances among endpoint changes, and the overlap of unavailable pairs. These discriminate persistence, common-visit strength and mixed loading signs without requesting study significance findings.
analysis_implications: Expected change means are fixed by supplied pre/post means in every scenario. Within-endpoint covariance changes the sampling variance of paired means and their t intervals. Shared visit structure changes latent-change associations: analytically target has common latent-change correlation 0.10/(1-0.65), stable_endpoint_specific has zero common latent-change correlation, and mixed_visit_response has signed magnitude 0.30/(1-0.35). These are implied latent assumptions, not observed source-scale correlations; differing lognormal transforms and marginal scales alter measured-scale results.
